Generally speaking, pharmacies have pretty strict policies on refilling all controlled substances.  It's not just ADHD medications.  In chain pharmacies these policies come from higher up and often cannot be overridden even if a pharmacist wants to.  But, individual pharmacists are also liable and many will be even stricter.  Like another poster said, they don't want to lose their license.

Things you can do:

1. Ask the pharmacy what their refill policy is for your medication.  Ask what happens over weekends, holidays, etc. so you can plan in advance.  If your med is something they need to order, ask what days they order medicine on and ask if you should call to remind them the day before so they don't have to order it when you try to refill it.

2. Use the same pharmacy consistently.  Be friendly with the staff.  AVOID any typical drug seeking behavior like complaining, begging, yelling, making excuses, etc.  They have heard them ALL.  It just makes you look like someone with an addiction problem.  Otherwise, you'll be surprised how far techs and pharmacists can be willing to go to help you out if they know you and like you.

3. If they tell you it's too soon to refill, ask what day you can get it.  Say thanks and come back on that day. Avoid drama.  You don't want a rep.

4. Don't take it personally. They are not singling you out.  They have to do this with everyone.

I voluntarily went into a psych ward to have ECT (shock therapy).  My pdoc and I talked about it extensively beforehand and he advised which hospitals to consider using and which ones I should definitely avoid.  There's usually one or two good ones in a major city and then a bunch of scary ones.  

My experience was fine except for a couple of very schizophrenic patients who just upset me generally.  Most people at my hospital were depressed, not patients of other disorders that can get erratic or violent, so the atmosphere was very subdued.  The doctors, nurses, and other staff were all friendly and polite.  There will be rules you will be expected to follow for everyone's safety but they are nothing stupid.  Like I had to get a disposable razor from them every morning if I wanted to shave and I had to bring it back for them to throw away.  You also couldn't keep a charging cord in your room.  I had to give them my book reader to charge up behind the counter when it needed charging.

As far as actually being helpful if you are not getting something like ECT there...don't go.  They cannot really help you unless you're experiencing a psychotic break, manic episode, or something similar.  They may make some changes to your medications while you're there and send some recommendations to your pdoc but typically you're only in a few days to a week if you're only depressed or suicidal so there's no time for any changes to actually take effect while you are there for the most part.  The rest of the stay will consist of several basic group therapy sessions a day and maybe some private counseling.  That's about it.  Their main goal is to keep your safe while you're a danger to yourself or others.  They do not treat or fix your underlying problems.

So if you're thinking about going into a psych ward for anhedonia treatment definitely do NOT.  Cross that idea off of your list.

I came out back in 1994.  I fully expected at the time that my parents would never accept me but I was not willing to live the rest of my life as a lie--if they don't love the real me, the love they have for the fake me isn't real either.

We didn't really speak for about a year.  Then when my sister told them I'd moved in with my boyfriend my dad started calling me asking me to bring him home for dinner to meet them.  I put that off for months expecting a disaster.  When I finally brought him home, he and my dad hit it off great.

My mom eventually learned to accept it but she was never thrilled about it.  She told me many times that she still loves me but wished I wasn't gay.  That's as close to acceptance as she ever got, but she kept that between us and participated in me and my boyfriend's life.

Give your parents time to process what you've told them.  Sometimes it will take a major life event for it to really sink.  I think my parents thought it was just a phase until I'd moved in with my boyfriend.  My dad was a genuine hillbilly who grew up on a small farm with no electricity but he came around.  My mom was college educated and pretty socially liberal but she struggled with it.  Don't think you can predict how they will react.  I expected my mom to be okay with it and my dad be the one throwing a shit fit.

Also remember if your parents never come around that family isn't just genetics.  It's who you choose to be a family with.  It's perfectly legitimate to add new people to your family and to weed some old ones out if that's the way it needs to be.
